mainTopic: Whether a כוי (a goat-deer hybrid) counts as a farm animal: its status for אותו ואת בנו, covering its blood on יום טוב, and the כהן's gifts, and whether the father's species counts.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion: distinguishing signs (סימנין) count on a Torah level. Then a ברייתא records a dispute about אותו ואת בנו, the ban on slaughtering a mother and its offspring on one day. חכמים apply it to a כוי, and רבי אליעזר does not. רב חסדא says the disputed כוי comes from a goat and a deer. The גמרא shows that the case is a hybrid daughter slaughtered with her own son. The רבנן count the father and hold that 'partly a שה' is enough. A משנה forbids slaughtering a כוי on יום טוב and covering its blood. From it, the גמרא learns that the רבנן are only in doubt whether the father counts. A ברייתא about the כהן's gifts then forces the גמרא to say that רבי אליעזר is also in doubt. The amud ends by asking what the two sides disagree about if both share the same doubt. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Distinguishing signs count on a Torah level
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous discussion: this position also holds that סימנין are valid on a Torah level.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he holds that distinguishing signs are valid by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the previous discussion. It adds one more point about the view it was explaining: signs can be relied on even for a Torah-level law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא used physical signs to identify an animal's parentage. This line says those signs are strong enough to rely on even where a Torah prohibition is at stake, not only a rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: Distinguishing signs (physical features used to identify something)
From the Torah; valid by Torah law

phrases.english: And distinguishing signs are by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Distinguishing signs can be relied on even for Torah-level prohibitions.

steps.title: A ברייתא: does אותו ואת בנו apply to hybrids and to a כוי?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say אותו ואת בנו applies to both כלאים and a כוי. רבי אליעזר says it applies to a goat-sheep hybrid but not to a כוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים taught: The law of אותו ואת בנו applies to hybrids and to a כוי. רבי אליעזר says: a hybrid from a goat and a ewe is covered by the law, but a כוי is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens a new topic. It is a dispute about whether the law against slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day covers mixed animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees about a hybrid of two farm animals, a goat and a sheep, because both parents are domesticated. The dispute is only about the כוי, an animal with a wild side to its parentage. The תנא קמא includes it, and רבי אליעזר leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah prohibition against slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day
A hybrid: an animal born from two different species
An animal of uncertain status, between a farm animal and a wild animal
Applies; is in effect

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The law of "it and its offspring" applies
to hybrids and to a koy.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְאַיִם הַבָּא מִן הָעֵז וּמִן הָרָחֵל –
phrases.english: a hybrid that comes from a goat and a ewe:
"it and its offspring" applies to it;

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי – אֵין אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ נוֹהֵג בּוֹ.
phrases.english: a koy: "it and its offspring" does not apply to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: אותו ואת בנו applies to כלאים and to a כוי. רבי אליעזר: it applies to a goat-sheep hybrid but not to a כוי.

steps.title: רב חסדא defines which כוי is under dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the disputed כוי is the animal born from a male goat and a doe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Which כוי do רבי אליעזר and חכמים argue about? The one that comes from a male goat and a doe.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא clarifies the ברייתא. He tells us which animal the word כוי refers to in this dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat is a farm animal and a deer is a wild animal, so their offspring is half and half. This explains why its status is unclear and why the two views argue about it.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagreed
A male goat
A doe (female deer)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Which koy is it
that Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages disagree about?

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַבָּא מִן הַתַּיִישׁ וּמִן הַצְּבִיָּיה.
phrases.english: It is the one that comes from a male goat and a doe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵיזֶהוּ כּוֹי שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בּוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term כוי from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disputed כוי is the offspring of a male goat and a doe.

steps.title: How exactly does this case happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact circumstances of the case רב חסדא described.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next moves. Which parent is the goat and which is the deer?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this law is about a mother and its offspring, it matters which animal is the mother. The גמרא will now test both possible arrangements.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the case look like? What are the exact circumstances?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case defined by רב חסדא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which parent is the goat and which is the deer, given that the law concerns the mother and her offspring.

steps.title: First option: a doe mother, but everyone exempts that case
steps.stepSummary: If the mother is a doe and the father a goat, רב חסדא himself says everyone agrees there is no liability, so there would be no dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a male goat mated with a doe, she gave birth, and one slaughters her and her child: but רב חסדא said that everyone agrees that when the mother is a doe and her offspring is from a goat, he is exempt! The Torah said 'a sheep and its offspring,' not 'a deer and its offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option: the mother is a doe. It rejects this option, because another ruling of רב חסדא says everyone agrees about that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'שה... and its offspring,' so the mother must be a farm animal. A doe is a wild animal, so everyone exempts this case. That leaves nothing for רבי אליעזר and חכמים to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion about to be rejected)
Everyone agrees
Exempt; not liable
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
A sheep or goat, a domesticated animal

phrases.english: If you say it is a male goat that mated with a doe,
and she gave birth, and he slaughters her and her child:
but didn't Rav Chisda say:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּהִיא צְבִיָּיה וּבְנָהּ תַּיִישׁ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees where she is a doe and her offspring is a goat
that he is exempt!
The Merciful One said "a sheep and its offspring,"
and not "a deer and its offspring"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first answer to היכי דמי and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב חסדא's כוי as the offspring of a doe mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא himself says everyone exempts a doe mother, since the verse requires the mother to be a שה. So there could be no dispute in this case.
steps.confusionAlert: The law follows the MOTHER. The verse names the mother as a שה, so what matters is whether the mother is a farm animal. The father's species is not the key question.

steps.title: Second option: a goat mother, but everyone obligates that case
steps.stepSummary: If the mother is a goat and the father a deer, רב חסדא says everyone agrees he is liable, so again there would be no dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a deer mated with a female goat, she gave birth, and one slaughters her and her child. But רב חסדא said that everyone agrees that when the mother is a goat and her offspring is from a deer, he is liable! The Torah said 'שה', and 'its offspring' means any offspring at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite arrangement: the mother is a goat. This also fails, because רב חסדא says everyone agrees on this case too. The next step answers this with a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mother is a farm animal, which fits the word שה. The verse puts no limit on the offspring, so everyone holds him liable. Both options lead to cases where everyone agrees, so the גמרא still has to explain what the dispute is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (offers a new suggestion after the first one failed)
A female goat
Liable
Whatever it is; any kind at all

phrases.english: Rather, it is a deer that mated with a female goat
and she gave birth, and he slaughters her and her child.
But didn't Rav Chisda say:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּהִיא תְּיָישָׁה וּבְנָהּ צְבִי –
phrases.english: everyone agrees where she is a goat and her offspring is a deer
that he is liable,
the Merciful One said "a sheep,"
and "its offspring" can be anything!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the reverse arrangement after step 5 failed, and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב חסדא's כוי as the offspring of a goat mother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat mother fits 'שה', and the offspring can be anything, so everyone obligates this case. Again there is nothing to dispute.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule from רב חסדא: the mother must be a farm animal (שה), and the offspring can be anything. A doe mother means everyone exempts; a goat mother means everyone obligates. So the גמרא still has to find where the dispute about the כוי really lies.

steps.title: The real case: the hybrid daughter and her son
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about a goat-and-doe daughter who gives birth to a son, where someone slaughters the daughter and her son on one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, the case is a male goat that mated with a doe. She gave birth to a daughter, that daughter gave birth to a son, and someone slaughters the daughter and her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the two challenges from steps 5 and 6 by giving a new case. In this case חכמים and רבי אליעזר really can disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 used the doe as the mother, and step 6 used the goat as the mother, and neither left room for a dispute. Now the mother is the hybrid daughter herself, and she is slaughtered together with her own son. The question becomes whether this daughter counts as a שה, since her father is a goat and her mother is a wild doe.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It opens an answer that keeps the earlier idea but explains it a new way.
A male goat, which is a domesticated animal (בהמה).
A doe, a female deer, which is a wild animal (חיה).
He slaughters her and her son on the same day.

steps.confusionAlert: The animal being judged here is the daughter, not her son. She is the כוי (half goat, half deer), and she is now the mother in the אותו ואת בנו case.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a male goat that mated with a doe,
and she gave birth to a daughter,
and the daughter gave birth to a son,
phrases.notes: This daughter is the כוי: her father is a goat and her mother is a deer.

phrases.english: and he slaughters her and her son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 5–6 by defining a new case where a dispute is possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's case seemed to be the כוי slaughtered with its own mother or father, where everyone agrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is the כוי as a mother, slaughtered together with her own son.

steps.title: The two reasons behind the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן count the father and say 'even partly a שה' is enough. רבי אליעזר rejects both points.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that we take the father's line into account, and that 'שה' includes even an animal that is only partly a שה. רבי אליעזר holds that we do not take the father's line into account, and we do not say 'even partly a שה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by explaining why each side rules the way it does in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the daughter's goat father makes her partly a domesticated animal. Being partly a שה is enough for אותו ואת בנו to apply. רבי אליעזר ignores the father, so she counts only as her deer mother's child, and he does not apply the law to a partial שה.

keyTerms.meaning: We take the father's line into account when deciding an animal's status.
The word in the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו (ויקרא 22:28) referring to a domesticated animal.
Partly a שה, meaning only part of the animal's makeup is domesticated.

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן need two ideas to apply the law here: the father counts, and 'partly a שה' is enough. רבי אליעזר rejects both.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: we take the father's line into account,
and 'sheep' means even partly a sheep.
phrases.notes: The word שה comes from the פסוק about not slaughtering a mother and her young on one day.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer holds: we do not take the father's line into account,

phrases.aramaic: וְ״שֶׂה וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת שֶׂה״ – לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: and we do not say 'sheep, even partly a sheep.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of each side in the case set up in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the dispute through two underlying principles
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute rests on two questions: does the father count, and is 'partly a שה' enough.

steps.title: Why not argue about the father question alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the dispute is not simply about counting the father, as in the dispute between חנניה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them argue just about whether we take the father's line into account, which is the dispute between חנניה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of case. If the father question is part of the argument, why not argue about it in a simple case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a known dispute between חנניה and the רבנן about whether the father's line counts. The גמרא asks why חכמים and רבי אליעזר needed a complicated hybrid case instead of just repeating that disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them argue instead about. This form introduces a suggestion for a better case.
A dispute.

phrases.english: But let them argue about whether we take the father's line into account,
which is the dispute between Chananya and the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: That is a separate dispute about whether a father and his offspring may be slaughtered on one day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why the dispute in steps 7–8 is placed in this complicated case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the hybrid case as the setting for the dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If counting the father is the issue, a simpler and already known case would show the dispute.

steps.title: The hybrid case teaches 'even partly a שה'
steps.stepSummary: Arguing about the father alone would not teach that the רבנן also hold 'even partly a שה' counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they argued only about that issue, I would have thought that in this case even the רבנן agree we do not say 'even partly a שה'. So the case teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hybrid case teaches something new: the רבנן's second principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Arguing about the father alone shows only that the רבנן count the father. You might still think a goat-deer mix does not count as a שה at all. Placing the dispute in this case shows that for the רבנן, partly a שה is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought. It introduces a mistaken idea that the text comes to rule out.
They agree.
It teaches us something new.

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is placed in this case to show that the רבנן hold two ideas: the father counts, and even partly a שה is enough.

phrases.english: If they argued about that, I would have thought:
in this case even the Rabbis agree

phrases.aramaic: דְּ״שֶׂה וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת שֶׂה״ לָא אָמְרִינַן,
phrases.english: that we do not say 'sheep, even partly a sheep,'
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the chosen case teaches an extra point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even the רבנן might not count an animal that is only partly a שה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן hold that even partly a שה is subject to אותו ואת בנו.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about slaughtering a כוי on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, and if it was slaughtered, its blood is not covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the משנה that says: you may not slaughter a כוי on יום טוב, and if you did slaughter it, you do not cover its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems hard to fit with what we just learned about the רבנן. This line sets up the challenge, which the גמרא spells out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the כוי as a doubtful animal. On יום טוב, covering the blood means moving earth, which is only allowed for a מצוה we are sure about. So the ruling hints at a doubt, while we just said the רבנן count the father outright.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status is unclear: it may be a domesticated animal (בהמה), a wild animal (חיה), or both
A Festival day, when some kinds of work are forbidden
We do not cover its blood (the מצוה of כיסוי הדם applies to wild animals and birds)

phrases.english: But that which we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אוֹתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: A כוי may not be slaughtered on יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שְׁחָטוֹ – אֵין מְכַסִּין אֶת דָּמוֹ.
phrases.english: and if one slaughtered it, one does not cover its blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a משנה to test the conclusion of steps 8 and 10 that the רבנן count the father.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן clearly count the father's species
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats the כוי as uncertain, which does not seem to fit a clear rule.

steps.title: If the mother is a deer, everyone would require covering
steps.stepSummary: If the כוי comes from a male goat and a female deer, both sides agree it counts as a deer, so it could be slaughtered and its blood covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is the משנה talking about? If it is a male goat that mated with a female deer and she gave birth, then according to both the רבנן and רבי אליעזר, you should be able to slaughter it and cover the blood, since it is a deer, or at least partly a deer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out which case the משנה could mean. It shows that a כוי with a deer mother cannot be the case, because everyone would allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the mother counts. A deer mother makes the כוי at least partly a wild animal, so covering its blood is a sure מצוה. Then there is no reason to forbid slaughtering it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (offers a possible case, often about to be rejected)
A male goat
A female deer (doe)
Part of, partly

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא בְּתַיִישׁ הַבָּא עַל הַצְּבִיָּיה וְיָלְדָה,
phrases.english: If we say with a male goat that mated with a doe, and she gave birth,
whether according to the רבנן or according to רבי אליעזר,
let him slaughter and cover,
for it is a deer, and even partly a deer is enough.
phrases.notes: Its mother is a deer, so at the very least it is partly a deer. That is enough to make covering the blood a sure מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּתַיִישׁ הַבָּא עַל הַצְּבִיָּיה וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the challenge of step 11 by ruling out one possible case.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as a case where the mother is a deer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here there is no doubt at all, so the משנה's strict ruling could not be talking about this case.

steps.title: If the father is a deer, neither view fits the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If the כוי comes from a male deer and a female goat, the רבנן would require covering and רבי אליעזר would allow slaughter without covering. Neither view forbids slaughtering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be a male deer that mated with a female goat and she gave birth. But according to the רבנן, he should slaughter and cover. According to רבי אליעזר, he should slaughter and not cover.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other case, where only the father is a deer. It shows that neither the רבנן nor רבי אליעזר would say what the משנה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן surely count the father, the כוי is partly a deer, so covering is a sure מצוה‎. רבי אליעזר ignores the father, so the כוי is simply a domesticated animal and needs no covering. Both views give a clear answer, so neither explains why the משנה forbids slaughtering it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A female goat
Let him slaughter and not cover the blood

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּצְבִי הַבָּא עַל הַתְּיָישָׁה וְיָלְדָה,
phrases.english: Rather, with a deer that mated with a female goat, and she gave birth,
if according to the רבנן, let him slaughter and cover,
phrases.notes: The רבנן count the father, so the deer father makes it partly a wild animal.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – לִשְׁחוֹט וְלָא לִיכַסֵּי.
phrases.english: if according to רבי אליעזר, let him slaughter and not cover.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּצְבִי הַבָּא עַל הַתְּיָישָׁה וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the deer-mother case, tries the deer-father case and finds it also does not fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as a deer-father case, according to either opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each opinion gives a clear ruling, while the משנה's ruling only makes sense if the case is doubtful.

steps.title: The רבנן are unsure whether the father counts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is a deer-father case, and it follows the רבנן, who are in doubt whether the father's species counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is a male deer that mated with a female goat. The רבנן are unsure whether we take the father's species into account or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The רבנן do not count the father for sure; they are only in doubt about it, and that doubt explains the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it is unclear whether the כוי is partly a wild animal, covering its blood is only a possible מצוה. So we should not slaughter it on יום טוב at the start. If someone already did, we do not move earth to cover the blood for a מצוה that may not apply. This sharpens the earlier picture: the רבנן's view about the father is a doubt, not a clear rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (keeps the case that was just rejected and explains it differently)
They are in doubt about it
We take the father's species into account

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, whether the father counts is only a doubt. That is why a כוי from a deer father and a goat mother is not slaughtered on יום טוב, and its blood is not covered if it was.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with steps 8 and 10, where it sounded like the רבנן surely count the father. Here we learn they only worry that it might count; they are not certain.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the כוי's doubtful status and why a doubtful מצוה cannot override the rules of יום טוב.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a deer that mated with a female goat,
and the רבנן are in doubt
whether we take the father's species into account
or we do not take it into account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 11 to 13 by keeping the deer-father case and explaining the רבנן's view as a doubt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the strength of the רבנן's position: a doubt, not a certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן surely count the father, so a deer-father כוי would clearly need covering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן are unsure whether the father counts, so the כוי is a doubtful case and the משנה's strict ruling follows.

steps.title: For רבי אליעזר, the father clearly does not count
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן are unsure whether the father's species counts, it follows that רבי אליעזר is sure it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן are in doubt about the father, but for רבי אליעזר it is obvious that the father does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the answer in step 14. This conclusion also prepares the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are only in doubt about the father, yet they still apply אותו ואת בנו to the כוי, to be safe. רבי אליעזר says the law does not apply to a כוי at all, so he is not ruling from a doubt. For him the father's species clearly does not count, and the animal simply follows its mother.

keyTerms.meaning: They are in doubt; they are unsure
It is obvious to him; he has no doubt
An animal whose status is unclear; here, one born from a deer and a goat

phrases.english: And from the fact that the Rabbis are in doubt,
phrases.notes: They are unsure whether we pay attention to the father's species. That was the answer in step 14.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Eliezer it is obvious.
phrases.notes: Obvious to him that the father does not count at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדִּלְרַבָּנַן מְסַפְּקָא לְהוּ, לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 14's answer and lays the ground for a new challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבנן: in doubt about the father's species. רבי אליעזר: the father's species certainly does not count.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the כהן's gifts from a כוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. The רבנן say the gifts for the כהן apply to a כוי, and רבי אליעזר says a כוי is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a ברייתא: the foreleg, jaws, and maw must be given from a כוי and from hybrids. רבי אליעזר says a sheep-goat hybrid must give the gifts, but a כוי is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to clash with what we just said. This step sets up the challenge; the problem itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא is the רבנן, and they require the gifts from a כוי. רבי אליעזר agrees that a goat-sheep mix gives the gifts, since both parents are the right kind of animal. A כוי, though, is exempt in his view. The גמרא will now ask how the רבנן can require the gifts if they are unsure about the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Foreleg, jaws, and maw: the parts of a slaughtered animal given to a כהן
The gifts owed to the כהן
A mixed breed; here, a goat and sheep mix
Apply; are in force

phrases.english: But that which was taught in a ברייתא:
The foreleg, the jaws, and the maw
apply to a koy and to hybrids.
phrases.notes: This first opinion is the רבנן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְאַיִם הַבָּא מִן הָעֵז וּמִן הָרָחֵל –
phrases.english: A hybrid that comes from a goat and a ewe
is obligated in the gifts,
from a koy, it is exempt from the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be tested against the conclusion of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusions of steps 14 and 15: the רבנן are in doubt about the father's species, and רבי אליעזר is sure it does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each possible case fails for one side. With a goat father, the רבנן's 'obligated' is too strong for a mere doubt (step 18). With a deer father, רבי אליעזר's 'exempt' does not fit if he surely ignores the father (step 20).

steps.title: Testing the case of a male goat and a female deer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of כוי the ברייתא means. It tries a male goat with a female deer, and shows that רבי אליעזר's exemption fits this case well.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? If it is a male goat that mated with a female deer, רבי אליעזר's exemption makes sense: he does not accept 'even partly a שה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is talking about and tries one option. It explains רבי אליעזר's side first, as a setup for the problem with the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother is a deer, which owes no gifts. For רבי אליעזר the father does not count, and he does not hold that 'partly a שה' is enough. So this כוי is just a deer and is exempt. That part works smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (a suggestion that will be tested)
Granted; this part works fine
'שה' includes even an animal that is only partly a שה
Male goat / female deer

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. In step 14 the father was a deer. Here the father is a goat and the mother is a deer.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵימָא בְּתַיִישׁ הַבָּא עַל הַצְּבִיָּיה וְיַלְדָּה,
phrases.english: If you say with a male goat that mated with a female deer, and she gave birth,
granted, according to Rabbi Eliezer, who exempts,
he holds that 'a sheep, and even partly a sheep'
phrases.notes: The gifts פסוק says 'שור או שה' (דברים 18:3).

phrases.english: we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּתַיִישׁ הַבָּא עַל הַצְּבִיָּיה וְיַלְדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to set up the case of the ברייתא from step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of כוי the ברייתא is discussing
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A first suggestion is a goat father with a deer mother. It fits רבי אליעזר; the test for the רבנן comes next.

steps.title: Why should the owner give anything, according to the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: Even if the רבנן hold 'partly a שה,' the deer half is surely exempt. The goat half depends on the father, which is only a doubt. So the owner could tell the כהן: 'Bring proof that the father counts, and take.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the רבנן: granted they hold 'even partly a שה.' He clearly does not give half. For the other half, let him tell the כהן: 'Bring proof that we consider the father, and then take it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן's ruling in the ברייתא. If they are only in doubt about the father, the owner should not have to give the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's half is a deer, so it owes nothing. The father's half is a goat, but the רבנן are unsure whether the father counts. When there is a doubt about money, the one who wants to take it must bring proof. So the כהן should get nothing, yet the ברייתא says the gifts apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Even granting; let us accept that
Half
Bring proof and take: whoever wants to take money must prove his claim
We take the father's species into account

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge uses a basic money rule: someone who wants to take money from another must bring proof. The rule shows that a doubt cannot force the owner to pay.

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
granted that they hold 'a sheep, and even partly a sheep,'
granted, half he does not give him,
phrases.notes: The mother's half is a deer, which owes no gifts. 'Him' is the כהן.

phrases.english: for the other half, let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The owner speaks to the כהן about the goat half, which comes from the father.

phrases.english: Bring proof that we are concerned with the father's seed,
and take.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the attack set up in steps 16 and 17. The goat-father case cannot explain the רבנן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as a goat-father, deer-mother case according to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן are in doubt about the father. With a money doubt, the כהן must bring proof before he can take. So the owner should be exempt, but the ברייתא obligates him.

steps.title: A new case: a deer father and a goat mother
steps.stepSummary: To avoid the problem from step 18, the גמרא says the ברייתא's כוי comes from a male deer and a female goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is a deer that mated with a female goat, and she gave birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The goat-father case did not work, so the גמרא flips the parents. This line sets up the next move, where the new case gets tested against each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the mother is the goat, and a mother's species always counts. So the goat half is surely a שה. Only the deer half from the father is in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: a deer, a wild animal
a female goat
and she gave birth

phrases.english: Rather, with a deer that comes
upon a female goat, and she gives birth.
phrases.notes: Now the parents are reversed from step 17: the deer is the father and the goat is the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בִּצְבִי הַבָּא עַל הַתְּיָישָׁה וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the goat-father case, which failed in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means a goat father with a deer mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a deer father with a goat mother.

steps.title: The new case fits the רבנן but not רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, 'obligated' means half the gifts. But for רבי אליעזר, who supposedly ignores the father, the baby is a full goat and should owe all the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the רבנן: 'obligated' means obligated in half the gifts. But for רבי אליעזר, the owner should be obligated in all the gifts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new case on both sides. It works for the רבנן but creates a problem for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the goat half from the mother surely owes the gifts. The deer half from the father is a doubt, so the owner can say 'bring proof.' That leaves half the gifts. But step 15 said רבי אליעזר is sure the father does not count. Then the baby is just a goat and should owe everything, yet the ברייתא says he exempts it.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense (for one side, but…)
half of the gifts given to the כהן
all of the gifts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sides. Here the רבנן are the ones who say 'obligated' (only half), and רבי אליעזר is the one who says 'exempt.' The problem is that by his own view he should obligate fully.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the Rabbis,
what does 'obligated' mean? In half the gifts;
phrases.notes: The other half is the deer half from the father. That part is only a doubt, so the כהן can't force it.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Eliezer,
let him be obligated in all the gifts?
phrases.notes: This uses step 15's idea that רבי אליעזר ignores the father, so the baby is fully a goat like its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי חַיָּיב בַּחֲצִי מַתָּנוֹת אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לִיחַיַּיב בְּכוּלְּהִי מַתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new case from step 19 against both opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as a deer father and goat mother, together with step 15's claim about רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר ignores the father, a baby with a goat mother is a full goat and owes all the gifts. That clashes with his ruling of 'exempt.'

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is also unsure about the father
steps.stepSummary: The case really is a deer father and goat mother. Like the רבנן, רבי אליעזר is unsure whether the father's species counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is a deer that mated with a female goat. רבי אליעזר is also in doubt whether we take the father into account or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the deer-father case. It fixes the problem by taking back the idea that רבי אליעזר is sure the father does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 inferred that רבי אליעזר is sure the father does not count. That inference is now dropped. If he is also in doubt, the deer side is uncertain for him too, so he is not forced to obligate all the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (we keep the case we had)
he is in doubt about it
we take the father's species into account

steps.whyThisMatters: This takes back the inference from step 15. That is what sets up the next question about where the two sides really disagree.

phrases.english: Actually, with a deer that comes
upon a female goat, and she gives birth,
and Rabbi Eliezer too
is in doubt

phrases.aramaic: אִי חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב אוֹ לָא,
phrases.english: whether we take the father's species into account or not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בִּצְבִי הַבָּא עַל הַתְּיָישָׁה וְיָלְדָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר נָמֵי סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by changing how we understand רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר is sure the father's species does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר is also in doubt about the father's species.

steps.title: If both sides are unsure, what do they argue about?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן and רבי אליעזר are both in doubt about the father, the גמרא asks what their disagreement actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the רבנן are in doubt and רבי אליעזר is in doubt, what do they disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 21 creates a new problem. The גמרא asks what the point of the argument is, and it sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows a real disagreement: the רבנן say 'obligated' and רבי אליעזר says 'exempt.' If both start from the same doubt, the גמרא must find some other point that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: but since
about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: But since the Rabbis are in doubt
and Rabbi Eliezer is in doubt,
about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּלְרַבָּנַן מְסַפְּקָא לְהוּ וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 21's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 21 that רבי אליעזר is also in doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both sides hold the same doubt, they should rule the same way. The ruling of 'exempt' against 'obligated' then has no explanation.
